reason: The passage (2 Samuel 13) depicts a failure of leadership, not a model for good leadership. King David is manipulated into allowing his son Amnon to have access to Tamar under false pretenses. After Amnon sexually assaults Tamar—a vulnerable member of his household—David hears of the incident and becomes angry, but the text indicates he takes no decisive action to protect her welfare, seek justice, or hold his son accountable. Tamar is left desolate and dishonored. Rather than exemplifying leadership that cares for the welfare of vulnerable people, the narrative demonstrates the harmful consequences when a leader fails to protect those under his authority, particularly vulnerable women in his own family.
